chunks: And Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, known as Ibn Maqbara al-Qazwini, narrated to us this hadith, saying: He informed us that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn Hasan ibn Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) said: He told me that Muhammad ibn Ali al-Hashimi said: He narrated to us that Isa ibn Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) said: He told me his father, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), who said:

When Fatima (peace be upon her) was about to die, she called me and said: Are you to fulfill my testament and covenant? He said: I said: Yes, I will fulfill it. She then bequeathed to me and said: If I die, bury me at night, and do not give permission to the two men whom she mentioned. He said: Then, when her illness became severe, the women of the Muhajirun and the Ansar gathered to her and said: How have you become this morning, O daughter of Allah's Messenger, from your illness? She said: I have become, by Allah, one who will leave this world of yours, and he mentioned the hadith similarly.
ai.seo_question: What were Fatima's final instructions regarding her burial and the two men to be excluded?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the intimate transmission chain (isnad) linking Fatima al-Zahra directly to Ali ibn Abi Talib, emphasizing the authenticity of her final wishes. Her instruction to bury her at night and exclude two specific men is widely interpreted by Shia scholars as a subtle political statement regarding the legitimacy of the Caliphate and the exclusion of those who disputed Ali's right to leadership. The dialogue with the women of the Muhajirun and Ansar further underscores the distinction between the Ahl al-Bayt's spiritual status and the broader community's political realities during her illness.
